parties:
Golak Chandra Roy ------ Appellant
vs.
Niva Rani Guha Roy ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
In this Lawazima matter we are called upon to decide as to whether in this First Miscellaneous Appeal which arises out of an application for revocation of a Probate an advalorum court fee is to be paid on the memo of appeal or not. 

 2. The respondent filed Probate Case No. 6/82 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka. The Probate Case was allowed on 16.9.82. Thereafter the present appellant filed the revocation Case No. 147/82 for revocation of the Probate granted in that Probate proceeding. This revocation case was dismissed as not maintainable. Against that order the present First Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellant before this court. 

 5. At the out set it is to be stated that Chapter 34 of Civil Rules and Orders deals with periodical re- turns and statements submitted by the Civil Courts. In such submission the classification of cases are made as suits; appeals arising from decrees, Miscellaneous judicial cases, Miscellaneous non-judicial cases and Miscellaneous appeals. The statements of cases are filed by the Civil courts to the Supreme Court, High Court Division for the purpose of ascertaining the disposal of the various nature of cases by civil courts below. The suits and appeals from decrees arc classified in one group and the Miscellaneous judicial cases, Miscellaneous non-judicial cases and Miscellaneous appeals arc classified in another group only for the purpose of satisfaction of this court as to the disposal of the various nature of cases by the civil court below. Rule 773 speaks that an application for Probate or for letters of administration should be considered as a Miscellaneous judicial case until the date upon which it is contested and it will be treated as a suit from the day when it is contested. Thus as per Rule 773 when a case for Probate or for letters of administration is contested it be- comes a suit and when not contested it becomes a Miscellaneous judicial case for the purpose of judging the return of the civil court for ascertaining whether a suit or a Miscellaneous case has been disposed of by the court below. In a contested case a longer time is taken and the higher court will treat it as if a regular suit has been disposed of. Rule 773 is only for the limited purpose of Judging the disposal list and nothing beyond. Rule 773 (note II) also speaks that application for revocation of Probate and letters of administration should be treated in the same manner as an application for Probate or letters of administration. We have no hesitation in our mind that this classification is only for the limited purpose of submitting report to the higher court and as such from this it will be totally erroneous to hold that the order passed in a revocation proceeding is a decree. Herein we will consider some decisions to see the impact of an order in such a proceeding. In a case reported in A.I.R. 1928 Allahabad-51, Sulaiman, J observed that Probate is a Miscellaneous judicial case and in a Probate proceeding the applicant is called the petitioner. In that decision it has been observed as follows: 

 6. In another decision reported in I.L.R. Bombey 33-256 it has been clearly held that the proceedings for Probate are not of a regular suit or that they shall be treated as such for all purposes. A Probate proceeding does not under the law, fall within the description of a regular suit and they shall take as nearly as may be the form of a suit, according to the Provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure. This would show that Probate Proceeding does not, under the ordinary case, fall within the description of a regular suit. In that decision it has further been observed that the Legislature intended the difference to exist due to the special provision’s in the Court Fees Act (Act VII of 1870) for the valuation of Court fee in the case of an application for Probate as distinguished from a suit. 

 7. In another case reported in 9IC.-538 it has been noted in clear language that one is not to pay ad valorem court fee on a memorandum of appeal against a probate proceeding. Their Lordships observed as follows :- 

 "The court fee payable on a memorandum of appeal against an order in probate proceedings is governed by Article I of Schedule II of the Court Fees Act. Therefore, an advalorum stamp duty on the value of the e state need not be levied in such cases". 

 8. We will further refer to the different provisions of the Court-fees Act to see whether the observation made in the note sheetic correct or not. In Article 11 of Schedule I it has been stated that Probate of a will or letters of administration when the amount or value of the property in respect of which the grant of probate or letters is made exceeds of Tk. 2, 000/- on such amount or value upto Tk. 10,000/- then two per centum (proper fees) is to be paid. Article 11 goes on speaking different valuations of the estate and proper fees which is to be given on the estate. This Article applies where stamp duty is pay- able on the amount or value of the property when Probate or letters of Administration is granted by a Court. This Article lays down the fee payable for the Probate of will or letters of administration and not the fee payable on an application in such grant which is provided for by Article 1 of Schedule II of the Court fees Act. Herein we will consider section 19 of the Court fees Act. Section 19(1) speaks of payment of court fees in respect probate and letters of administration. In that section it has only been stated that no order for probate or letters of ad- ministration can be granted unless a valuation of the property is given as set forth in the 3rd schedule and the court is satisfied with the fees mentioned in article No. II of the I Schedule has been paid on such valuation. That is to say that in a probate proceeding the valuation of the property must be given as contemplated in schedule III of the Court-fees Act. So that after a probate is granted necessary and proper fees can be realised under Article 11 of Schedule I of Court Fees Act. The application that is filed in a probate proceeding is in the nature of a Miscellaneous judicial case and for that court fee is to be paid as required for application or petition as contemplated in the Article I(a) of schedule II Court fees Act. The appeal that has been filed before this court is against an order and it is governed by Article 11 Schedule II namely, Memorandum of Appeal presented against an order to a High Court. The learned Advocate submits that he has paid court fee of taka 10/- which is required in such Memorandum of Appeal before this court. 

 9. Thus we are of the opinion that no further court fee is to be paid on this memo of appeal. The court fee payable on a memorandum of appeal against an order in a probate proceeding according to us is governed by Article 11 of Schedule II of the Court Fees Act. The Office is directed to follow this observation hereinabove for such cases future guidance.
